subject: Hydra Analytics POC — success specs, timeline, and next steps

Subject: Hydra Analytics POC — success specs, timeline, and next steps

Thanks for the call today — good alignment overall. Per our discussion, I pulled together the concrete success criteria and a proposed 4-week evaluation plan so we have something to sign off on before we spin up the sandbox. Please review and call out any hard constraints.

High-level success criteria (agreed so far):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 200 ms for 512-token sequences under baseline load.
- Throughput: sustain 50 inference requests/sec with <2% request error rate.
- Cost: effective cost <= $0.003 per input token (after batching and prefix caching). We will share the cost model and token accounting used.
- Quality: pass rate >= 88% on your set of 150 critical queries (we'll run blind human eval + automated checks). Hallucination incidents <= 1% on those queries.

Proposed 4-week plan (compact):
Week 0 (integration prep): exchange sample workloads, provide sandbox credentials, install test harness.
Week 1 (baseline): run current prompts on Redwood baseline model variants and measure latencies/cost.
Week 2 (tuning): iterate batching/quantization profiles, KV caching, and routing policies.
Week 3 (stress): run sustained throughput tests and run failure/fallback scenarios.
Week 4 (readout): joint readout + decisions (go/no-go/next steps).

Owners:
- Redwood SE: Diego Fernandez (integration, testing shepherd)
- Redwood CS/Infra: Ben Carter (ops, infra tuning)
- Redwood Security/Provisioning: Kimberly Park (sandbox, policy)
- Hydra: Alex + Priya (sample datasets, acceptance sign-off)

Next steps I can action this week:
1) Attach mutual-action-plan.xlsx (detailed checkpoints) and poc-sample-load.csv (sample payloads).
2) Provision temporary sandbox; will send link + creds after you confirm scope of data retained.
3) Ben will prepare an infra checklist for throughput windows.

Questions for you: can you confirm a list of 150 critical queries and whether any require PHI handling? Also confirm your preferred readout window on the week of Apr 18.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

---
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — this is very helpful. Quick notes from our side after regrouping: 
- The latency and throughput targets look reasonable, but our procurement/legal team needs to see the data retention and SOC2 evidence before we send real customer payloads. Can Kimberly point us to the SOC2 summary and retention guarantees?
- On quality: we were hoping to target a >=90% pass rate on the 150 critical queries; can your blind eval process run a separate tighter slice of ~30 user-critical queries for that threshold?
- Token cost: our internal finance model looks at end-to-end cost per user interaction rather than per token; can you share a one-page breakdown that maps your per-token model to per-interaction (we've attached a small sample payload file for reference).

Attached: hydra_sample_payloads.json (small set of 25 representative requests).

If we can get SOC2 evidence and your cost mapping today, we can confirm the 150-query set and lock the kickoff for Mon Apr 18.

—Alex

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alex. Short answers below and actions we took: 
- SOC2 / retention: Kimberly — can you drop the SOC2 summary and a short retention FAQ for Hydra? (Kimberly: tagging you to this thread).
- Tight quality slice: yes — we can run the 30 user-critical queries with a tighter acceptance threshold of 90% and include the blind human eval results in the readout.
- Cost mapping: attached is a one-page cost mapping (short explainer) and we used the payloads you attached to estimate token counts. Note our per-token model assumes batching improvements and prefix caching; we'll show both raw and optimized per-interaction numbers.

Sandbox provisioning: I created temporary sandbox instructions and a provisioning link (internal link below) — we will not accept production customer data in the sandbox until we have formal DPA in place. Please confirm the test data will be synthetic or anonymized.

Attachment: poc-runbook.md (run command examples, perf test steps).

Ben: I flagged the infra windows for the week of Apr 18 — can you confirm the 2-hour sustained throughput slot on Apr 20?

Diego
